_comment: Contracts that are declared but have no producing code yet.
ADR-0002 makes contract-first a rule: a schema lands as its own reviewed change,
with a version bump, BEFORE any code implementing it. That rule collides with the
schema-coverage check in test/contract-conformance.test.ts, which requires every
schema on disk to be validated against a value the running system produced.
Both are right. This file is the seam between them: a schema listed here is
exempt from needing a produced value, and says why and what will produce it.
Two rules keep it from becoming a place schemas go to be forgotten, matching the
- an entry with no reason or no `produced_by` fails;
- an entry whose schema HAS a conformance case is stale and fails, so the
exemption cannot outlive the implementation it was waiting for.
Five of the original seven entries have been removed because the evaluation pipeline
now produces them: configuration, eval-suite, eval-case, eval-run and comparison are
validated in test/contract-conformance.test.ts against values a real run emitted.
The two below remain because a judge adapter and a promotion path do not exist yet.

judge-verdict was removed on 22 August 2026: the judge adapter exists (application/src/judge.ts, guarded by core/src/eval/judge-policy.ts) and test/contract-conformance.test.ts now validates a verdict it produced. Landing the schema first worked exactly as intended -- runs, disagreement_rate, position_randomized and a declared agreement threshold were mandatory before anyone wrote a judge that would otherwise have omitted them.

pending.reason: Written by the release pipeline when a run is promoted to a frozen reference. The evaluation pipeline produces runs now, but no promotion path exists and none should until an anchor suite does.
